topics.title: Me, and a website about circuits

slides.title: Me, and a website about circuits
slides.subtitle: The unglamorous version of the journey

slides.title: What I actually did for 2.5 years
slides.caption: Pushed on Friday at 5 PM. Shocked, shocked, when it broke over the weekend.

box.content: The CV says "integrated RFID systems." The reality was closer to this:

list.text: 150+ production issues diagnosed and closed, mostly at hours I would rather forget.
Byte-level UID and CSN conversion — because two readers from two vendors never agree on endianness.
RS-232 timeouts that behaved perfectly in the lab and failed only on site, only on Fridays.
SQL deadlocks under load, offline sync that lost transactions, thermal printers with opinions.

note.text: None of this was in a tutorial. All of it is what the job actually is.

slides.title: What is Circuit Digest, really?
slides.caption: The actual feature graphic. SMS, plate reads, barcode scans, GPS pins.

box.title: circuitdigest.com — published by Semicon Media, Coimbatore

list.text: One of the most-read electronics and embedded systems publications online.
Build guides for Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, STM32 — real circuits, real code, real photos.
Component explainers, datasheets in plain language, and honest hardware reviews.
Read by students, hobbyists, and working engineers in more countries than I can list.

slides.title: Circuit Digest Cloud — what I build now
slides.imageAlt: Cartoon of a tiny ESP32 chip lifting a barbell of data up to a smiling cloud
slides.caption: An ESP32 has about 320 KB of RAM. This is roughly how the upload feels.
slides.content:
Tutorials are one half. Infrastructure is the other.

Circuit Digest Cloud handles: device provisioning and fleet management, MQTT telemetry with live dashboards, and alerts over email, SMS, and WhatsApp.

slides.title: What that actually looks like
slides.caption: No cartoon this time. This is circuitdigest.cloud, live, right now.

box.content:
135 projects active in the last 24 hours. 249 weekly active users. 6,331 community members building with it.

One platform to analyse, control, and connect — that is the actual tagline, not something I made up for this slide.

slides.title: The stack, minus the buzzwords
slides.caption: The real API catalog. Messaging, vision, tracking, pick one, it is live in minutes.

list.text: FastAPI + PostgreSQL + MQTT for ingestion and device-facing APIs.
GPS tracking with polygon geofencing and live maps.
Computer vision for number-plate, helmet, and object detection, plus live video.
Shipped on DigitalOcean with GitHub Actions and Sentry watching for the 2 AM surprises.

slides.title: GeoLinker, for real
slides.caption: A real tracker on a real walk around Coimbatore. 7.18 km, 26 minutes.

box.content:
GeoLinker is the GPS tracking piece of Circuit Digest Cloud: live position, route history, and polygon geofencing, plotted on an actual map.

This is not a mockup. It is one of our own trackers, walking the streets near the office.

slides.title: From breadboard to dashboard
slides.caption: ESP32, a SIM800L module, a fistful of jumper wires, and a phone showing it worked.

box.content:
This is the whole job, honestly. A breadboard held together with hope and rubber bands on one side, a live map with your data on it on the other.

Everything in the tools section exists to make the wiring side faster, not to replace it.

slides.title: What that dashboard actually looks like
slides.caption: Live camera, live chart, live controls. The boxes in that diagram are real.

box.content: Colour pickers for the lights, a slider and a gauge for room temperature, a WebRTC camera feed, and a 24-hour chart, all updating from actual MQTT messages.

slides.title: We already put an agent in it
slides.caption: "Which of my devices are offline?" It just answers. In IST, unprompted.

box.content:
This is not a hypothetical. Circuit Digest Cloud already ships an AI assistant you can ask about your devices in plain English — over WhatsApp, no less.

Which is a convenient place to stop talking about Circuit Digest and start talking about how this became possible at all.

topics.title: From autocomplete to whatever this is

slides.title: From autocomplete to whatever this is
slides.subtitle: A short, opinionated history

slides.title: A very short history
slides.caption: The last panel is not a joke. Someone in this room will do this by Friday.

list.text: Autocomplete era: it finished your line. Sometimes correctly.
Chat era (2022): you asked, it answered, you copied and pasted and prayed.
Editor copilots: it moved into the IDE and could see your open file.
Agent era (now): it reads the repo, runs the tests, reads the errors, and tries again.

slides.title: A chatbot vs an agent
leftPoints: You copy, paste, wire it up, and verify
Great for learning and getting unstuck
One turn at a time, you drive every step
rightPoints: Reads files, runs commands, edits code directly
Plans, acts, checks the result, corrects itself
Can read docs and confirm its own work
Chases a goal across many steps

note.text: Claude Code, Antigravity, and Codex are all in the right-hand column. That is the shift.

slides.title: The colleague who never sleeps and never brings snacks
slides.imageAlt: A frazzled four-armed robot coding at 2:47 AM surrounded by coffee cups
slides.caption: 2:47 AM. Fourth coffee. "Project: almost done." It is not almost done.
slides.content:
The word that matters is agency

A chatbot can explain a bug to you. An agent can open the file, reproduce the bug, patch it, run the suite, and hand you a diff. Same underlying model. Completely different thing to work with.

slides.title: Hot take
slides.caption: "Sleep is optional." "Deploy on Friday?" This wall is the argument for AI, not against it.

box.content:
Most "AI will replace developers" posts are written by people who have never been paged at 3 AM to fix a data migration.

The job was never typing. It is deciding what to build, and being the person who understands the system when it breaks. AI moves the typing. It does not move the responsibility.

slides.title: Adoption, roughly
slides.caption: Every AI keynote has this exact chart. Here is ours, for compliance.

box.content:
I could show you a real adoption number. You would forget it by the next slide, so here is the honest version instead.

In 2022, using AI at work was a party trick. In 2026, not using it is the thing that gets a comment in code review. That is the whole trend.

slides.title: The skill that matters now
slides.caption: "Algorithms and Suffering" is not a real book. It should be. Fundamentals still win.

list.text: Prompting — giving enough context and clear constraints.
Verifying — reading output like you would review a stranger's PR.
Security sense — not pasting secrets, not trusting generated auth code blindly.

topics.title: Using it without making a mess

slides.title: Using it without making a mess
slides.subtitle: Where it helps, where it lies, and how to ask

slides.title: Old loop vs new loop
slides.caption: "PROJECT CHAOS (DOOMED)." This is the old loop, unfiltered.

list.text: Old: plan, write, test, review, deploy — every step by hand.
New: same steps, but an agent drafts, explains, and tests alongside you, while you decide what "correct" means.

slides.title: Where it pulls its weight vs where it lies
leftPoints: Explaining a codebase you were just handed
First-draft tests for code that already works
Debugging with a real stack trace in hand
rightPoints: Architecture and trade-offs — it will pick one and defend it
Security review — it misses the subtle holes, cheerfully
Domain judgement — it does not know your users or your rules
"Is this actually correct" — only you and the tests can answer that

note.text: It is never unsure. That is the dangerous part.

box.title: Same request, very different afternoon
box.code:
// Vague - invites guessing
"fix my code"

// Specific - grounded in reality
"In src/api/users.py, GET /users/{id} returns 500
when id is not numeric. Traceback below. Add
validation that returns 400 with a clear message,
matching validate_order_id() in src/api/orders.py.
<paste traceback>"

slides.title: Before you let it near main
slides.caption: This is not a workflow. It is a confession with extra steps.

list.text: Read every line. Do not merge what you have not read.
Actually run it. Do not just nod at it.
Grep for keys, tokens, and hardcoded credentials.
Be able to explain it — in review, in a viva, in an interview.

note.text: Rule of thumb: if you would be embarrassed to have written it, do not ship it under your name.

slides.title: The human stays in the loop
slides.imageAlt: A team meeting where the whiteboard reads AI DO NOT TOUCH MAIN BRANCH and a cheerful robot says I CAN DO THAT
slides.caption: The whiteboard says do not touch main. The robot says "I can do that." Your job is to stay between them.
slides.content:
Every workflow here has a human checkpoint

That is not overcaution. It is the line between using AI as a tool and quietly outsourcing your judgement to it.

slides.subtitle: What each one is, and when to reach for it

slides.title: What we will actually look at
slides.caption: The temptation is real. Finish the current project first.

list.text: ESP-IDF — the framework ESP32 firmware is built in.
GitHub — repos, CI/CD, and where most AI tools plug in.
Google Antigravity — Google DeepMind's agentic IDE.
OpenAI Codex — OpenAI's cloud and CLI coding agent.
Claude Code — Anthropic's terminal-first agent.

slides.title: ESP-IDF — where the firmware lives
slides.imageAlt: Isometric cartoon of a circuit board drawn as a small town called Microville
slides.caption: Welcome to Microville, population 1024. Every IoT project starts in a town like this.
slides.content:
Espressif's official SDK for ESP32-class chips

  • Built on FreeRTOS — real multitasking on a microcontroller.
  • idf.py to build and flash, menuconfig for build options.
  • JTAG and OpenOCD for real debugging, not just serial-print archaeology.

slides.title: GitHub — the boring backbone that runs everything

list.text: Repos and pull requests — where review actually happens.
Actions — the pipeline that deploys Circuit Digest Cloud.
Copilot — inline, autocomplete-style suggestions.

slides.title: Before you start vibe coding
slides.imageAlt: Holographic software blueprints including PRD, User Flow, Architecture, and AI Rules on a modern development workspace
slides.caption: Specs and blueprints anchor the agent before code generation begins.

list.text: PRD — what to build
User Flow — how people move through it
UI/UX — how it looks
Tech Spec — how it is built
Database Schema — what data is stored
API Spec — how systems talk to each other
Security Rules — what must be protected
AI Coding Rules — how the agent should behave in your repo
Testing Plan — how you will know it works
Deployment Plan — how it actually ships

note.text: Minimum viable set: PRD, User Flow, Tech Spec, and AI Coding Rules. The other six can wait.

list.title: OpenAI Codex
list.text: Cloud + CLI agent. Runs in a sandbox and hands work back as a reviewable pull request. Best on well-scoped jobs.

list.title: Google Antigravity
list.text: Agentic IDE with browser sub-agents that verify UI changes visually, and deep whole-codebase context.
Reads and edits files, and runs your commands directly.
MCP lets it connect to external tools and data sources.
Plan mode proposes a plan for you to approve before it touches anything.

note.text: This deck was assembled with Claude Code, in this project's own repo.

slides.title: Top 6 Red Flags While Building Apps with Claude Code
slides.subtitle: Avoid these mistakes to keep your project fast, safe, and under control

list.title: Don't give the entire PRD/FRD document at once.
list.text: Dumping the whole spec into one prompt overwhelms the session and buries what matters. Break it into phases and feed it one phase at a time, like the build plan you already have.

list.title: Don't lose your prompt instructions — save them for later.
list.text: Keep every phase prompt written down somewhere outside the chat. If a session ends or you need to resume on a new machine, you should never have to reconstruct instructions from memory.

list.title: Don't waste your context window on unnecessary conversations.
list.text: Off-topic chatter, repeated explanations, and long unrelated debugging threads all eat into the context Claude Code needs to keep track of your actual project. Keep sessions focused.

list.title: Don't build everything before testing each phase.
list.text: Verify each phase against its own checklist before starting the next one. Skipping this lets small, easy-to-fix bugs quietly stack into large, hard-to-trace ones.

list.title: Don't let AI make all the architectural decisions.
list.text: Review and approve the important calls yourself — database design, security approach, tech stack, third-party services. Claude Code should implement your decisions, not just default to its own.

list.title: Don't skip Git commits after every working milestone.
list.text: Commit as soon as a phase works. Without that history, one bad change can undo hours of progress with no way back to a known-good state.

note.text: Six habits, one outcome: you stay in control of the build, not the other way around.

slides.title: Free tools, hackathons, and where to compete

box.title: The shortcuts nobody tells you about

list.text: GitHub Student Developer Pack — free Copilot, Codespaces, Azure credit, and every JetBrains IDE. Verify once at education.github.com.
Open source — search "good first issue" on GitHub, or wait for Hacktoberfest every October.
Hackathons — MLH and Devfolio for the weekend circuit, Smart India Hackathon for the real thing.
Competitions — Google Summer of Code if you want to get paid for open source, Kaggle if data is your thing.

note.text: Pick one of these to actually do this month. Bookmarking is not participation.

slides.title: If you remember four things
slides.caption: Do these four and the line goes up. Results may vary. Line not to scale.

list.text: Circuit Digest turns electronics knowledge into tutorials and real infrastructure.
AI moved from answering to acting. That is the whole story of the last two years.
Keep a human checkpoint before and after the agent acts.
ESP-IDF, GitHub, Antigravity, Codex, Claude Code — each solves a different slice.
